pages.footer: Introduction - Free to Read & Listen in 6 Languages
pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


When you first start following Jesus, you are excited. You are reading the Gospels. You are learning about grace. You are learning about forgiveness. You are learning about a relationship with God. It feels new. It feels fresh. It feels like a relationship.


Then you read the Old Testament. You read about festivals. You read about trumpets and tents and trumpets. You read about fasting and feasting. You read about blood and fire. You close the book. You think, "What does this have to do with my relationship with Jesus?"


I get it. I have been there. I have wondered why God gave so many festivals. I have wondered why they seem so strange. But here is the thing. Those festivals are not random. They are not just ancient history. They are a calendar. They are a rehearsal. They are a relationship. Every festival was pointing to Jesus. Every celebration was pointing to a relationship with Him.


This book is for you. You are new to the faith. You are trying to understand. You are trying to build a foundation. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 ancient festivals. We are going to see what they meant. We are going to see why they were given. And we are going to see how Jesus fulfilled every single one of them. We are going to see how the rituals pointed to a relationship.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not be confused by the Old Testament festivals. You will understand them. You will understand their purpose. You will understand their fulfillment. You will see that the festivals were never meant to be empty rituals. They were meant to be a relationship. And you will see that Jesus is the fulfillment of every festival. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for ...

pages.footer: Day 1 of 30 (Free Preview - Days 1 to 3 are Free)
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Israelites were slaves in Egypt. They cried out to God. God sent Moses. God sent plagues. The final plague was the death of the firstborn. But God gave a way out. Each family was told to kill a lamb. They were told to paint the lamb's blood on the doorposts of their houses. When the angel of death passed through Egypt, it would see the blood. It would pass over that house. The people inside would live. This is the Passover. It was a ritual. It was a reminder of deliverance.


The New Reality
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Jesus is the Passover Lamb. He died on the cross. His blood was shed. His blood was painted on the doorposts of our hearts. When judgment comes, it passes over us. We are saved by His blood. The festival of Passover was a rehearsal. The reality is Jesus.


Why It Matters For You
You are new to the faith. You are learning about salvation. You are learning about the cross. The Passover tells a story of deliverance. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are delivered. You are saved. You are passed over.


Faith Builder
Do you believe that Jesus is your Passover Lamb? Write down one thing you are thankful for about His sacrifice.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Passover Lamb. Thank you for shedding your blood for me. Thank you that the judgment has passed over me because of you. I am safe because of you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 1: The Passover

pages.subtitle: Free Sample Day (2 of 3)
pages.footer: Day 2 of 30 (Free Preview - Days 1 to 3 are Free)
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


When the Israelites left Egypt, they had to leave quickly. They did not have time to let their bread rise. They baked unleavened bread. It was flat. It was hard. It was the bread of haste. But God told them to keep celebrating this festival. For seven days every year, they were to remove all yeast from their homes. Yeast was a symbol of sin. It spreads. It puffs up. It was a reminder to live a holy life. It was a ritual.


The New Reality
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


Paul applies this to Jesus. He says we are to remove the yeast of sin from our lives. We are to live with sincerity and truth. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the unleavened bread. He is without sin. If we want to live like Him, we must remove the yeast.


Why It Matters For You
You are learning to live a holy life. You are learning to remove the things that separate you from God. The law of unleavened bread tells a story of purity. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you can live a holy life.


Faith Builder
What is the yeast in your life? What is the thing that puffs you up? What is the thing that spreads? Write it down. Ask God to help you remove it.


The Prayer
God, help me to remove the yeast from my life. Help me to stop tolerating the things that separate me from you. Give me a heart of sincerity and truth. Help me to live a holy life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 2: The Unleavened Bread

pages.subtitle: Free Sample Day (3 of 3)
pages.footer: Day 3 of 30 (Free Preview - Days 1 to 3 are Free)
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God." - Exodus 23:19 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The firstfruits was an offering. It was the first sheaf of the harvest. The Israelites were told to bring it to God. It was a sign of trust. It showed they believed God would provide the rest. But it was also a ritual. The firstfruits was a promise that a greater harvest was coming.


The New Reality
"But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." - 1 Corinthians 15:20


Jesus is the firstfruits. He is the first to rise from the dead. His resurrection is a promise that we too will rise. If the firstfruits is raised, the rest will be raised too. This is the hope of the Christian faith.


Why It Matters For You
You are learning about the resurrection. You are learning about eternal life. The firstfruits tells a story of hope. It tells a story of resurrection. Through Jesus, you have hope. You have eternal life.


Faith Builder
Do you believe in the resurrection? Write down one thing that gives you hope.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Thank you for the promise that we will rise too. Thank you for the hope of eternal life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 3: The Firstfruits

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Count off seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain. Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God by giving a freewill offering in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you." - Deuteronomy 16:9-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Weeks was a celebration of the wheat harvest. The people brought their firstfruits. They brought a freewill offering. They rejoiced before the Lord. It was a time of gratitude. It was a time of joy. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater harvest. It pointed to a greater outpouring.


The New Reality
"When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting." - Acts 2:1-2


The Feast of Weeks was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost. The Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples. The church was born. The harvest began. The freewill offering was not wheat. It was people. It was a harvest of souls.


Why It Matters For You
You are learning about the Holy Spirit. You are learning about the church. The Feast of Weeks tells a story of outpouring. It tells a story of harvest. Through Jesus, you have the Holy Spirit. You are part of the harvest.


Faith Builder
Do you want to be filled with the Holy Spirit? Write down one thing you want the Spirit to help you with.


The Prayer
Holy Spirit, thank you for being poured out on the day of Pentecost. Thank you for the harvest of souls. Fill me with your presence. Use me in your harvest. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The Feast of Weeks (Pentecost)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"On the first day of the seventh month hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. It is a day for you to sound the trumpets." - Numbers 29:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Trumpets was a call to attention. The trumpets were blown. The people gathered. They prepared for the Day of Atonement. It was a day of awakening. It was a day of preparation. It was a ritual. It pointed to a future call. It pointed to a future awakening.


The New Reality
"For the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first." - 1 Thessalonians 4:16


Jesus is the trumpet call. He will come down from heaven with a loud command. The trumpet will sound. The dead in Christ will rise. We will be gathered to Him. The Feast of Trumpets was a rehearsal. The reality is the return of Jesus.


Why It Matters For You
You are learning about the return of Jesus. You are learning about the future. The Feast of Trumpets tells a story of awakening. It tells a story of readiness. Through Jesus, you have hope. You have a future.


Faith Builder
Are you ready for the trumpet call? Write down one thing you want to do to be ready.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the trumpet call. Thank you for the promise of your return. Help me to be ready. Help me to be awake. Help me to be looking for you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The Feast of Trumpets

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must deny yourselves and not do any work—whether native-born or a foreigner residing among you—because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you." - Leviticus 16:29-30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Day of Atonement was a day of national cleansing. The high priest entered the Most Holy Place. He offered sacrifices for his own sin. He offered sacrifices for the sin of the people. The blood was sprinkled on the mercy seat. The people fasted. They waited. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater sacrifice. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"He did not enter by means of the blood of goats and calves; but he entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption." - Hebrews 9:12


Jesus is the Day of Atonement. He is the high priest. He is the sacrifice. He entered the Most Holy Place once for all. He obtained eternal redemption. The Day of Atonement was a rehearsal. The reality is the cross.


Why It Matters For You
You need atonement. You need cleansing. You need to be made right with God. The Day of Atonement tells a story of redemption. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are made right. You are cleansed.


Faith Builder
Do you need cleansing today? Write down one area of your life that needs God's cleansing.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Day of Atonement. Thank you for entering the Most Holy Place. Thank you for obtaining eternal redemption. Thank you for cleansing me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Live in temporary shelters for seven days: All native-born Israelites are to live in such shelters so your descendants will know that I had the Israelites live in temporary shelters when I brought them out of Egypt." - Leviticus 23:42-43 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Tabernacles was a reminder. It was a reminder of the wilderness. The people lived in tents. They remembered how God provided for them. They remembered how God was with them. It was a festival of joy. It was a festival of gratitude. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater dwelling. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


Jesus is the Feast of Tabernacles. He is the dwelling place of God. He is the glory. He is the presence. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He came to dwell among us. He came to be with us.


Why It Matters For You
You are learning about the presence of God. You are learning about relationship. The Feast of Tabernacles tells a story of dwelling. It tells a story of presence. Through Jesus, you have the presence of God. You have relationship.


Faith Builder
Do you want to experience the presence of God? Write down one way you can practice His presence this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Feast of Tabernacles. Thank you for dwelling among us. Thank you for being with me. Help me to experience your presence. Help me to live in your presence. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: The Feast of Tabernacles

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God." - Exodus 20:8-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath was a gift. It was a gift of rest. The people were told to stop working. They were told to stop striving. They were told to rest. They were told to trust. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater rest. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." - Matthew 11:28


Jesus is the Sabbath. He is the rest. He is the ceasing. He is the fulfillment of the Sabbath. He says, "Come to me. I will give you rest." Not the rest of a day. The rest of a lifetime. Not the rest of a ceremony. The rest of a relationship.


Why It Matters For You
You are tired. You are trying to earn God's love. You are trying to be good enough. The Sabbath tells a story of rest. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you can stop striving. You can rest.


Faith Builder
What are you striving for? Write it down. Give it to Jesus. Rest in Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, I am tired. I am weary. Thank you for being my rest. Thank you for being my Sabbath. Help me to stop striving. Help me to rest in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Sabbath

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Year of Jubilee was a year of freedom. It was a year of release. It was a year of restoration. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. Land was returned. It was a reset. It was a fresh start. It was a ritual. It pointed to a freedom that would come. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Jesus is the Jubilee. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the Jubilee. He proclaims good news to the poor. He proclaims freedom to the prisoners. He sets the oppressed free.


Why It Matters For You
You need freedom. You need release. You need restoration. The Jubilee tells a story of freedom. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are free. You are restored.


Faith Builder
What do you need freedom from today? Write it down. Give it to Jesus. He is your Jubilee.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Thank you for restoring me. Help me to walk in your freedom. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Year of Jubilee

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old. You may take it from the sheep or from the goats." - Exodus 12:5 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Passover lamb was a specific lamb. It had to be perfect. It had to be without blemish. It had to be killed. It had to be eaten. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a perfect lamb. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, 'Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!'" - John 1:29


Jesus is the Passover Lamb. He is the perfect lamb. He is the lamb without blemish. He is the lamb who takes away the sin of the world. He is the fulfillment of the Passover lamb.


Why It Matters For You
You need a substitute. You need someone to take your place. The Passover lamb tells a story of substitution. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have a substitute. He took your place.


Faith Builder
Do you need a substitute today? Write down one thing you need Jesus to take your place in.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Passover Lamb. Thank you for taking my place. Thank you for taking away the sin of the world. Thank you for being the perfect lamb. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Passover Lamb

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect or blemish and that has never been under a yoke." - Numbers 19:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The red heifer was a sacrifice for cleansing. The red heifer was taken outside the camp. It was killed. It was burned. Its ashes were collected. They were mixed with water. They were sprinkled on the people. They were cleansed. It was a ritual. It pointed to a cleansing that would come. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood." - Hebrews 13:11-12


Jesus is the red heifer. He suffered outside the city gate. He was burned. He was the ultimate cleansing. His blood cleanses us. His blood purifies us. He is the fulfillment of the red heifer.


Why It Matters For You
You need cleansing. You need purification. You need to be made holy. The red heifer tells a story of cleansing. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are cleansed. You are purified.


Faith Builder
What area of your life needs cleansing today? Write it down. Give it to Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the red heifer. Thank you for suffering outside the gate. Thank you for cleansing me. Cleanse my heart today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Red Heifer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Then the Jews celebrated the Feast of Dedication at Jerusalem. It was winter." - John 10:22 (Written around 90 A.D.)


The Feast of Dedication is also called Hanukkah. It celebrates the rededication of the temple. The temple had been defiled. It was cleansed. It was dedicated to God. It was a festival of light. It was a festival of freedom. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater temple. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"But when Jesus spoke these words, many believed in him." - John 8:30


Jesus is the Feast of Dedication. He is the temple. He is the light. He is the dedication. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He cleanses the temple. He dedicates it to God. He is the light of the world.


Why It Matters For You
You need to be cleansed. You need to be dedicated. The Feast of Dedication tells a story of dedication. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are cleansed. You are dedicated.


Faith Builder
Do you need to be dedicated to God? Write down one way you can dedicate your life to Him this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Feast of Dedication. Thank you for cleansing me. Thank you for dedicating me to God. Thank you for being the light of the world. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur. Because of all that was written in this letter, and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them, the Jews took it upon themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should continue to observe these two days as a celebration." - Esther 9:26-27 (Written around 400 B.C.)


The Feast of Purim celebrates the deliverance of the Jews from Haman. Haman wanted to destroy the Jews. Esther risked her life. The Jews were saved. It is a festival of deliverance. It is a ritual. It pointed to a greater deliverance. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of the Son he loves, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins." - Colossians 1:13-14


Jesus is the Feast of Purim. He is the deliverance. He is the rescue. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He rescued us from the dominion of darkness. He brought us into His kingdom. He is the greater deliverance.


Why It Matters For You
You need to be rescued. You need deliverance. The Feast of Purim tells a story of rescue. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are rescued. You are delivered.


Faith Builder
What do you need to be rescued from today? Write it down. Give it to Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Feast of Purim. Thank you for rescuing me. Thank you for delivering me from the dominion of darkness. Thank you for bringing me into your kingdom. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Feast of Purim

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Also at your times of rejoicing—your appointed festivals and New Moon feasts—you are to sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and they will be a memorial for you before your God. I am the LORD your God." - Numbers 10:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of New Moon was a monthly celebration. It marked the beginning of a new month. It was a time of renewal. It was a time of re-dedication. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater renewal. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!" - 2 Corinthians 5:17


Jesus is the Feast of New Moon. He is the renewal. He is the new creation. He is the fulfillment of the feast. In Him, the old has gone. The new is here. He makes all things new.


Why It Matters For You
You need a fresh start. You need renewal. The Feast of New Moon tells a story of renewal. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have a fresh start. You are made new.


Faith Builder
Do you need a fresh start today? Write down one thing you want God to renew in your life.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Feast of New Moon. Thank you for making all things new. Thank you for the fresh start. Renew my heart today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Feast of New Moon

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Live in temporary shelters for seven days: All native-born Israelites are to live in such shelters so your descendants will know that I had the Israelites live in temporary shelters when I brought them out of Egypt." - Leviticus 23:42-43 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Booths is another name for the Feast of Tabernacles. It was a reminder of the wilderness. The people lived in tents. They remembered how God provided for them. They remembered how God was with them. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater dwelling. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


Jesus is the Feast of Booths. He is the dwelling place of God. He is the glory. He is the presence. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He came to dwell among us. He came to be with us.


Why It Matters For You
You need to know that God is with you. You need to experience His presence. The Feast of Booths tells a story of dwelling. It tells a story of presence. Through Jesus, you have the presence of God.


Faith Builder
Do you know that God is with you? Write down one way you can remind yourself of His presence this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Feast of Booths. Thank you for dwelling among us. Thank you for being with me. Help me to experience your presence. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The Feast of Booths

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood and said in a loud voice, 'Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.'" - John 7:37 (Written around 90 A.D.)


The water libation was a ceremony during the Feast of Tabernacles. The priests would pour out water on the altar. It was a prayer for rain. It was a prayer for blessing. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater pouring out. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them." - John 7:38


Jesus is the water libation. He is the living water. He is the pouring out. He is the fulfillment of the water libation. He says, "If anyone is thirsty, come to me and drink." He gives rivers of living water.


Why It Matters For You
You are thirsty. You are thirsty for love. You are thirsty for peace. You are thirsty for joy. The water libation tells a story of satisfaction. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you can drink. You can be satisfied.


Faith Builder
What are you thirsty for today? Write it down. Ask Jesus to satisfy it.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the water libation. Thank you for being the living water. Thank you for satisfying my thirsty soul. Help me to drink from you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 16: The Water Libation

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"When Jesus spoke again to the people, he said, 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.'" - John 8:12 (Written around 90 A.D.)


The light ceremony was a celebration during the Feast of Tabernacles. The temple was lit with huge lamps. It was a reminder of the pillar of fire in the wilderness. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater light. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." - John 8:12


Jesus is the light ceremony. He is the light of the world. He is the fulfillment of the light ceremony. He is the pillar of fire. He is the light of life.


Why It Matters For You
You need light. You need guidance. You need direction. The light ceremony tells a story of light. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have light. You have guidance.


Faith Builder
Where do you need light today? Write it down. Ask Jesus to shine.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the light ceremony. Thank you for being the light of the world. Thank you for illuminating my path. Help me to walk in your light. Amen.
pages.title: Day 17: The Light Ceremony

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Then have the trumpet sounded everywhere on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the Day of Atonement sound the trumpet throughout your land." - Leviticus 25:9 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Jubilee trumpet was a signal. It announced the Year of Jubilee. It proclaimed freedom. It proclaimed release. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater freedom. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"For the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first." - 1 Thessalonians 4:16


Jesus is the Jubilee trumpet. He is the signal. He is the announcement. He is the fulfillment of the Jubilee trumpet. He will come with a loud command. He will come with the trumpet call of God. He will proclaim freedom.


Why It Matters For You
You need to be ready. You need to be listening. The Jubilee trumpet tells a story of readiness. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are ready. You are listening.


Faith Builder
Are you listening for the trumpet? Write down one thing you can do to be more ready.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Jubilee trumpet. Thank you for the promise of your return. Help me to listen. Help me to be ready. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: The Jubilee Trumpet

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Put the bread of the Presence on this table to be before me at all times." - Exodus 25:30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The shewbread was a symbol. It was a symbol of the presence of God. It was a symbol of the provision of God. It was a symbol of the bread of life. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live forever. This bread is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world." - John 6:51


Jesus is the shewbread. He is the bread of the presence. He is the bread of life. He is the fulfillment of the shewbread. He is the bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.


Why It Matters For You
You are hungry. You are hungry for the presence of God. You are hungry for the provision of God. The shewbread tells a story of provision. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are fed. You are satisfied.


Faith Builder
Are you hungry for God? Write down one way you can feed on His presence this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the shewbread. Thank you for being the bread of the presence. Thank you for being the bread of life. Feed me today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The Shewbread

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps." - Exodus 30:7 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The incense offering was a symbol. It was a symbol of prayer. It was a symbol of worship. It was a symbol of the presence of God. It was a sweet smell. It filled the temple. It rose to heaven. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"Another angel, who had a golden censer, came and stood at the altar. He was given much incense to offer, with the prayers of all God's people, on the golden altar in front of the throne." - Revelation 8:3


Jesus is the incense offering. He is the prayer. He is the worship. He is the sweet smell. He is the fulfillment of the incense offering. His prayers rise to heaven. His worship fills the temple. And now, because of Him, our prayers rise to heaven.


Why It Matters For You
You need your prayers to rise to heaven. You need your worship to be heard. The incense offering tells a story of prayer. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, your prayers rise to heaven.


Faith Builder
What do you want to pray about today? Write it down. Lift it to Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the incense offering. Thank you for being the prayer. Thank you for being the worship. Help my prayers to rise to heaven. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Incense Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Build an altar of acacia wood, three cubits high; it is to be square, five cubits long and five cubits wide." - Exodus 27:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The altar of burnt offering was the center of the tabernacle. It was where the sacrifices were made. It was where the blood was shed. It was where the fire burned. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater sacrifice. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"We have an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no right to eat." - Hebrews 13:10


Jesus is the altar of burnt offering. He is the sacrifice. He is the fire. He is the fulfillment of the altar. He is the place where sin is dealt with. He is the place where blood is shed. He is the place where fire falls.


Why It Matters For You
You need a sacrifice. You need a place to lay your sin. The altar tells a story of sacrifice. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have an altar. You have a place to lay your sin.


Faith Builder
What sin do you need to lay on the altar today? Write it down. Give it to Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the altar of burnt offering. Thank you for being the sacrifice. Thank you for dealing with my sin. Thank you for the fire. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The Altar of Burnt Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Put the altar in front of the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law—before the atonement cover that is over the tablets of the covenant law—where I will meet with you." - Exodus 30:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The altar of incense was in the Holy Place. It was where the priest burned incense. It was where the prayers of the people rose to God. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater prayer. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess." - Hebrews 4:14


Jesus is the altar of incense. He is the prayer. He is the worship. He is the fulfillment of the altar. He is the high priest. He is the one who intercedes for us.


Why It Matters For You
You need someone to pray for you. You need an intercessor. The altar of incense tells a story of intercession. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have an intercessor. He is praying for you.


Faith Builder
Do you need someone to pray for you today? Write down one thing you need Jesus to pray for.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the altar of incense. Thank you for praying for me. Thank you for interceding for me. Help me to pray. Help me to worship. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The Altar of Incense

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Make a bronze basin, with its bronze stand, for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it." - Exodus 30:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The laver was a basin of water. The priests washed their hands and feet before they entered the tabernacle. They had to be clean. They had to be pure. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater washing. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"But when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of righteous things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit." - Titus 3:4-5


Jesus is the laver. He is the washing. He is the cleansing. He is the fulfillment of the laver. He washes us. He cleanses us. He renews us by the Holy Spirit.


Why It Matters For You
You need washing. You need cleansing. You need renewal. The laver tells a story of cleansing. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are washed. You are cleansed.


Faith Builder
What do you need to be washed from today? Write it down. Give it to Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the laver. Thank you for washing me. Thank you for cleansing me. Thank you for renewing me by the Holy Spirit. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The Laver

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammer out its base and shaft, and make its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them." - Exodus 25:31 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The golden lampstand was a source of light. It was a source of illumination. It was a source of guidance. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"When Jesus spoke again to the people, he said, 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.'" - John 8:12


Jesus is the golden lampstand. He is the light. He is the illumination. He is the guidance. He is the fulfillment of the lampstand. He is the light of the world.


Why It Matters For You
You need light. You need illumination. You need guidance. The golden lampstand tells a story of light. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have light. You have guidance.


Faith Builder
Where do you need light today? Write it down. Ask Jesus to shine.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the golden lampstand. Thank you for being the light of the world. Thank you for illuminating my path. Help me to walk in your light. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The Golden Lampstand

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Make a table of acacia wood—two cubits long, a cubit wide and a cubit and a half high." - Exodus 25:23 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The table of showbread was a table. It held the bread of the presence. It was a symbol of the provision of God. It was a symbol of the presence of God. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty." - John 6:35


Jesus is the table of showbread. He is the bread of life. He is the provision. He is the presence. He is the fulfillment of the table. He is the bread that satisfies.


Why It Matters For You
You are hungry. You are hungry for the bread of life. The table of showbread tells a story of provision. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you are fed. You are satisfied.


Faith Builder
Are you hungry for Jesus? Write down one way you can feed on Him this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the table of showbread. Thank you for being the bread of life. Thank you for satisfying my hunger. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The Table of Showbread

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Have them make an ark of acacia wood—two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. Overlay it with pure gold, both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it." - Exodus 25:10-11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Ark of the Covenant was the most sacred object in the tabernacle. It held the tablets of the law. It held the manna. It held Aaron's staff. It was the place where God met with His people. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"And I saw the ark of his covenant in his temple, and there came flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake and a severe hailstorm." - Revelation 11:19


Jesus is the Ark of the Covenant. He is the law. He is the manna. He is the staff. He is the meeting place. He is the fulfillment of the ark. He is the presence of God. He is the throne of grace.


Why It Matters For You
You need to meet with God. You need to experience His presence. The Ark of the Covenant tells a story of meeting. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you meet with God. You experience His presence.


Faith Builder
Do you want to meet with God today? Write down one way you can meet with Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Ark of the Covenant. Thank you for being the meeting place. Thank you for being the presence of God. Help me to meet with you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Ark of the Covenant

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Make an atonement cover of pure gold—two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide." - Exodus 25:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The mercy seat was the lid of the Ark of the Covenant. It was where the high priest sprinkled the blood on the Day of Atonement. It was the place of atonement. It was the place of mercy. It was a ritual. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of his blood—to be received by faith." - Romans 3:25


Jesus is the mercy seat. He is the atonement. He is the place of mercy. He is the fulfillment of the mercy seat. His blood was sprinkled. His sacrifice was made. He is the place where justice and mercy meet.


Why It Matters For You
You need mercy. You need atonement. You need a place of grace. The mercy seat tells a story of mercy. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have mercy. You have atonement.


Faith Builder
Do you need mercy today? Write down one area of your life where you need God's mercy.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the mercy seat. Thank you for being the atonement. Thank you for being the place of mercy. Thank you for the blood that was sprinkled. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The Mercy Seat

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"And make two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover." - Exodus 25:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The two cherubim were on top of the mercy seat. They faced each other. Their wings spread out. They represented the presence of God. They were a ritual. It pointed to a greater presence. It pointed to Jesus.


The New Reality
"And he made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in Christ, to be put into effect when the times reach their fulfillment—to bring unity to all things in heaven and on earth under Christ." - Ephesians 1:9-10


Jesus is the two cherubim. He is the presence. He is the unity. He is the fulfillment of the cherubim. He brings unity to all things. He brings heaven and earth together. He is the presence of God.


Why It Matters For You
You need unity. You need connection. You need the presence of God. The two cherubim tell a story of unity. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have unity. You have connection.


Faith Builder
Do you feel disconnected from God? Write down one way you can reconnect with Him this week.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the two cherubim. Thank you for being the presence. Thank you for bringing unity. Thank you for connecting me to God. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The Two Cherubim

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"Celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of the crops you sow in your field." - Exodus 23:16 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Weeks was a celebration of the harvest. The people brought their firstfruits. They brought a freewill offering. They rejoiced before the Lord. It was a time of gratitude. It was a time of joy. It was a ritual. It pointed to a greater harvest. It pointed to a greater outpouring.


The New Reality
"When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting." - Acts 2:1-2


The Feast of Weeks was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost. The Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples. The church was born. The harvest began. The freewill offering was not wheat. It was people. It was a harvest of souls.


Why It Matters For You
You are part of the harvest. You are part of the church. The Feast of Weeks tells a story of outpouring. It tells a story of grace. Through Jesus, you have the Holy Spirit. You are part of the harvest.


Faith Builder
Do you want to be part of the harvest? Write down one person you can share Jesus with this week.


The Prayer
Holy Spirit, thank you for being poured out on the day of Pentecost. Thank you for the harvest of souls. Fill me with your presence. Use me in your harvest. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Feast of Weeks

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Ritual
"The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming—not the realities themselves." - Hebrews 10:1 (Written around 60 A.D.)


The rituals were shadows. The festivals were shadows. The celebrations were shadows. But the reality is Jesus. The reality is a relationship.


The New Reality
"Then I heard what sounded like a great multitude, like the roar of rushing waters and like loud peals of thunder, shouting: 'Hallelujah! For our Lord God Almighty reigns. Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.'" - Revelation 19:6-7


Jesus is the ultimate relationship. He is the wedding of the Lamb. He is the marriage supper. He is the relationship that never ends. He is the fulfillment of all the festivals. He is the reality. He is the relationship.


Why It Matters For You
You have a relationship. You have Jesus. You do not need to keep looking at rituals. You can live in the relationship. You can live in the reality. You can live in Christ. And one day, you will celebrate with Him forever.


Faith Builder
How has your relationship with Jesus grown over the last 30 days? Write down one thing you have learned.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the ultimate relationship. Thank you for being the wedding of the Lamb. Thank you for the relationship that never ends. Help me to live in the joy of your presence. Help me to celebrate you every day. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Relationship Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 ancient festivals. Now what? I challenge you to read the book of Revelation. It is 22 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It will show you how the festivals are fulfilled in the ultimate celebration. As you read, look for the shadows. Look for the substance. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The rituals are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The rituals point to a person. The rituals point to Jesus. You can understand the rituals and still miss the relationship. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The rituals are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: The Shadow and the Savior
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Shadow and the Savior takes a 30 day look at how the Old Testament points to your new life. It is for the new believer who wants to go further.
